items.title: Debian 13.8 bundles kernel and Chromium security fixes with a 122-package bugfix list
items.summary: Debian 13.8 has been released, bundling kernel and Chromium security fixes along with a 122‑package bug‑fix list. The update covers Debian Security Advisories DSA‑6408 to DSA‑6629, including patches for Chromium, Firefox ESR, and other components.

items.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
items.summary: GL.iNet confirmed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote‑management service to deploy custom malware on customers’ routers and KVM devices. The malware provides backdoors and reverse shells, giving attackers remote access.

items.title: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach
items.summary: Cleverbridge announced a data breach in which attackers stole customers’ payment card information, including credit card numbers and CVV codes.

items.title: FBI Investigating Apparent Hack of Its Key National Criminal Justice Database, AP Source Says
items.summary: FBI is investigating an alleged hack of its national criminal justice database. The incident involves a key law enforcement data repository. SecurityWeek reports the investigation is underway.

items.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets
items.summary: Rackspace warned customers of a breach in its Rackspace Spot cloud platform. Hackers used compromised credentials to deploy unauthorized workloads and access Kubernetes secrets. Customers were advised to review access controls.

items.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
items.summary: Microsoft reported a data breach where attackers exploited a vulnerability in Entra Connect Health, accessing administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data.

items.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests
items.summary: The BADBOX malware, targeting Android TV boxes, has resumed large‑scale ad‑fraud operations, generating an estimated 40 billion ad requests per day.

items.title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database
items.summary: The FBI’s National Crime Information Center was reportedly breached, marking a second incident in two months and potentially compromising law‑enforcement data sharing.

items.title: President Trump Taps Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director
items.summary: President Trump appointed Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director. Davies will lead the administration's cyber strategy. The appointment aims to strengthen national cyber defenses.

items.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
items.summary: A malicious webpage can extract Meta Muse private chats and stored memories without triggering an approval prompt, and could also access credentials stored by the assistant. The demonstration was limited to a single user and did not target real accounts.

items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.summary: GnuPG warns that a long user ID in an OpenPGP key can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, potentially exposing application data. Fixed versions are available and the flaw affects all software using GPGME before 2.3.0.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities – Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter – to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list after evidence of active exploitation, including CVE-2026-129448 with a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
items.summary: The CTO and co‑founder of ransomwarehelp.com has been charged with wire fraud after the company was found to pay attackers for decryption keys and charge victims a markup for services that were never performed.

items.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
items.summary: PHP 8.6 introduces stricter default behaviors to reduce potential attack vectors. The update removes permissive settings that previously allowed unsafe code execution.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: The Largest Squid Ever Filmed
items.summary: The article documents the filming of the largest squid ever captured near Japan’s Ogasawara Islands in December 2006. It also references unrelated security stories and blog moderation policy.

items.title: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists
items.summary: Unit 42 analyzes Com affiliate vishing attacks targeting healthcare and finance. The post offers actionable defense guidance against cloud data theft and extortion campaigns.

items.title: West Virginia Legislature hit with cyber incident affecting IT systems
items.summary: A cybersecurity incident disrupted IT systems at the West Virginia Legislature starting Thursday. The disruption was contained and did not spread to other government entities.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
items.summary: Researchers found that stolen Visa and Mastercard data included information useful for phishing but did not contain financial details. The data could aid attackers in credential harvesting.

items.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
items.summary: A China‑nexus threat group likely had a VMware vCenter zero‑day ready during the latest major update cycle. The group targeted VMware vCenter to exploit known vulnerabilities.

items.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
items.summary: Signal criticized Apple, Google, and Microsoft for not providing adequate AI agent controls. The company emphasized protecting user privacy against intrusive AI features.

items.title: US companies’ use of Chinese open weight AI draws rebuke from House chairmen
items.summary: House Homeland Security Committee investigated U.S. companies using low‑cost open‑weight AI models. The inquiry highlighted potential security risks associated with these models.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Signal blocks Apple, Google AI screenshotting in response to ‘existential threat’ to privacy app
items.summary: Signal now blocks screenshots by Apple, Google, and Microsoft AI agents to protect user privacy. The move follows a similar block implemented for Microsoft last year.

items.title: Container Store restores systems after cyberattack
items.summary: The Container Store’s parent company, Neighborhood Intelligence, announced that the retailer restored its website and systems after a weekend cyberattack. The incident was contained with no reported data loss.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: n0n extortion gang leaks data of JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers
items.summary: The extortion group n0n breached third‑party service providers for JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard, leaking customer data online. The leak includes personal and financial information of customers of the three major financial firms. The incident highlights the risk of third‑party vulnerabilities.

items.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
items.summary: Bell Canada confirmed a breach on November 17, 2026 by an 'agentic' threat actor that stole enterprise customer data, including information from a system used to order and provision telecom circuits. The attack targeted internal systems and exposed sensitive customer details. Bell is investigating the scope of the data loss.

items.title: In Security, Words Matter as Much as Tools, Maybe More
items.summary: Cyber leaders emphasize that clear, disciplined communication is a frontline defense in cloud security and AI adoption. The article argues that effective messaging can mitigate risks as much as technical controls. It calls for better communication practices across enterprises.

items.title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
items.summary: Meta’s WhatsApp fixed three security vulnerabilities, one affecting Android that may have been used in scam messages. The CVE‑2026‑23871 flaw involved incomplete validation of external ad‑reply URLs. The patch addresses the issue in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android.

items.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
items.summary: Threat actors employed the open‑source AI penetration‑testing framework Cairn to discover a zero‑day vulnerability in a medical imaging application. The vulnerability allowed them to take control of the server. The incident demonstrates the risk of AI tools in adversarial use.

items.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
items.summary: Chinese threat actors used AI agents that adapted for nearly a full day without human input to locate and exploit a zero‑day in a university server. The attack persisted until the vulnerability was discovered. The case shows autonomous AI capabilities in cyber attacks.

items.title: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
items.summary: Amazon reported that a China‑linked threat actor used the open‑source AI tool Cairn to attack two universities, potentially discovering a zero‑day bug. The attackers persisted in the attack, exploiting the vulnerability to gain control. The incident highlights the misuse of AI tools for exploitation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: What We Missed: Nvidia CEO Scandal Rocks AI Industry
items.summary: The video discusses recent news missed by the publication, including the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Microsoft cloud outage. The segment covers industry impacts and reactions. It provides context on recent AI industry developments.

items.title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
items.summary: Researchers identified the Bazuka Android malware framework that uses fake screen overlays to conceal credential theft and remote device control. The malware integrates large language models for victim management. It was discovered during an investigation of an NFC‑relay banking Trojan.

items.title: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
items.summary: The Dutch data protection authority warned that AI glasses misinterpret medication instructions and other scenarios, posing safety risks. The devices could lead to incorrect usage or harm. The watchdog urges caution and further safety testing.

items.title: NSA resumes normal operations following internal network disruptions
items.summary: NSA has resumed normal operations after internal network disruptions. Some facilities remain in Code Orange, delaying openings for non‑essential staff. Employees must check in with supervisors.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: WhatsApp Fixes Flaw Uncovered While Disrupting Scam Campaign
items.summary: WhatsApp discovered and fixed CVE‑2026‑23871, a vulnerability that could have made scam messages more credible. The flaw was identified by WhatsApp’s security team during a scam campaign disruption.

items.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
items.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase reported a data breach at a third‑party service provider. The breach exposed personal and marketing data of Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers.

items.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
items.summary: Storing passwords in spreadsheets can hide weak, reused, or compromised credentials. Centralized password management improves visibility, identifies risks, and simplifies secure sharing.

items.title: Spy court blasts UK secrecy, forces government to admit Apple ‘backdoor’ demand
items.summary: A UK spy court criticized government secrecy and forced an admission of an Apple backdoor demand. The court noted the notice could be acknowledged without compromising national security, but details remain undisclosed.
